---
title: "With polars extension (.mlf)"
toc: true
---

`mlfeatures` ships an opt-in [polars](https://docs.pola.rs/) accessor for fitting and applying steps in one expression, without writing out a `Recipe`. Importing `mlfeatures.polars` registers the `mlf` accessor on polars DataFrames. The accessor is polars-only: for pandas data frames, use a `Recipe`.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs

import mlfeatures.polars  # registers the `df.mlf` accessor

orders = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "city": ["NYC", "LA", "NYC", "SF", "LA", "SF"],
        "price": [10.0, 20.0, None, 30.0, 25.0, 12.0],
        "qty": [2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 4],
    }
)

orders.mlf.step_dummy(cs.string())
```

Notice that `.step_dummy()` returned a new DataFrame with a column for each level of `city` except the first (`LA`), which is the reference level that all-zero indicators stand for. Use `step_one_hot` to get a column for every level.

In the following sections we'll show some of the more useful steps to use directly on a polars DataFrame.

## Fit and apply happen together

Every `df.mlf.step_*()` call builds the step, fits it on the data frame, transforms that same data frame, and returns the result. The fitted step is discarded, so nothing the step estimated (a median, the levels of a column, PCA loadings) can be reused on other data. Calling the accessor again on a test set re-estimates everything from the test set, which is train/serve skew.

The accessor is for trying a step out and for one-off transforms. Whenever the same transform has to be applied to data you have not seen yet, build a `Recipe` and fit it once.

## Handle missing values: `step_impute_median`

`step_impute_median` fills nulls with the column's median (`step_impute_mean` and `step_impute_mode` are the other flavors):

```{python}
filled = orders.mlf.step_impute_median(cs.by_name("price"))
filled
```

## Multivariate feature engineering: `step_pca`

`step_pca` replaces numeric columns with their projection onto principal components (here on the imputed data frame, since PCA needs complete data):

```{python}
(
    orders
    .mlf.step_impute_median(cs.by_name("price"))
    .mlf.step_pca(cs.numeric(), num_comp=2)
)
```

## Chaining and other steps

The accessor is available on every result, so calls chain, as above. `df.mlf.apply()` takes any step objects, which reaches steps that have no `step_*` wrapper and custom steps. Each step is fitted in order on the data frame the previous one produced:

```{python}
from mlfeatures import Selectors as s
from mlfeatures import StepImputeMedian, StepNormalize

orders.mlf.apply(
    StepImputeMedian(s.numeric_features()),
    StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()),
)
```
